messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer `acme-prod` (Private/VPC) reporting intermittent 503s from behind our internal NLB. Ticket #5482 opened. Target group shows targets unhealthy intermittently.

maria: Any recent config changes on the cluster or envoy?

alex: No deploys in window. This is an internal NLB in front of Envoy (k8s service type: NodePort -> NLB). Envoy routes to service by DNS SRV (we use internal DNS for service discovery).

liam: Logs? envoy admin /clusters output?

alex: Pasted quick repro from a node in the same private subnet:

```
$ dig +short @10.1.2.5 service-api.acme.internal
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short @10.1.2.5 service-api.acme.internal
; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

And envoy admin shows the cluster with no endpoints:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/clusters | sed -n '1,120p'
cluster: service_api
  lb_endpoints: 0
  update_failure_state: false
```

When upstream endpoints are missing Envoy immediately serves 503 for requests.

sre-ana: That dig timeout suggests DNS egress is the problem. Is the VPC using a forwarder that sits on-prem? If so, egress rules need to allow UDP/TCP 53 to that forwarder.

maria: Can you show iptables/egress / firewall logs? Maybe the customer's egress allowlist dropped queries after a recent policy change.

alex: Ran tcpdump, picked a sample:

```
$ sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -vv port 53 and host 10.1.2.5
15:12:03.123456 IP 10.2.3.20.54012 > 10.1.2.5.53: 12345+ A? service-api.acme.internal. (37)
15:12:03.124001 IP 10.1.2.5 > 10.2.3.20: ICMP 10.2.3.20 udp port 54012 unreachable, length 48
```

So the DNS resolver host (10.1.2.5) is responding ICMP unreachable — suggests a firewall or security appliance blocking/blackholing UDP 53.

liam: Are health checks from the NLB using a hostname? NLB TCP health checks are IP-level, but since Envoy itself depends on DNS to populate upstreams, the path breaks higher up.

alex: Exactly. NLB sees Envoy NodePort unhealthy because Envoy returns 503 (no backends). NLB health of the node then flips. We saw timestamps line up with a recent firewall rule push on customer side at 15:10 UTC.

sre-ana: Short-term mitigation: change envoy cluster type to static IPs (if feasible) or temporarily configure healthcheck on NLB to TCP 443 to bypass L7 failure detection. For most customers we recommend making the health check hit an internal static endpoint that doesn't require service discovery.

maria: Can customer patch their egress allowlist quickly? Which IP(s)/ports do they need to open?

alex: They need to allow UDP and TCP 53 to the corporate DNS forwarder(s) and allow our internal resolver IPs. From inside the VPC the resolver IPs were `10.1.2.5` and `10.1.2.6` (customer-provided forwarders). Also allow outbound to our telemetry endpoints because our gossip/updates hit them (but the immediate fix is DNS).

support-bot: Related KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/dns-egress-allowlist — steps to validate and whitelist resolvers. :link:

liam: For escalation notes: collect `dig` failure outputs, `tcpdump` evidence, envoy admin snapshot, and NLB target group health events. If customer wants, we can schedule a quick window to flip the health check to TCP and monitor.

alex: I've attached logs to ticket #5482 and asked customer to open a firewall change (they confirmed they pushed a deny rule by mistake). They've queued a rollback.

sre-ana: After they roll back, verify with:
```
dig +short @10.1.2.5 service-api.acme.internal
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/clusters | grep -A3 service_api
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.14:443 -servername service-api.acme.internal
```

If those show valid IP answers and envoy shows endpoints, we should see 200s return and NLB health recover.

maria: Thanks — I'll mark this as P1 and ping customer success to confirm the rollback window. :thumbsup:

alex: Update 15:18 UTC — customer reverted the change, dig now returns IPs, envoy shows 3 lb_endpoints, NLB target group health flipping back to healthy in the next 2 mins. Closing loop once stable.

oncall-bot: Incident note auto-saved to #incidents/2026-03-17-5482. :white_check_mark:

alex: Closing thread — root cause: egress firewall change blocked DNS to the customer's forwarder, which starved Envoy of service discovery leading to 503s and NLB target health churn. Recommended long-term: healthcheck design that doesn't rely on runtime DNS (static probe endpoint) and an egress allowlist test plan.
